name: format_document

description: Propose whole-file formatting as one changes document, including empty successful edits. positions_degraded:response means inexact edit columns. full defaults false; true adds exact normalized raw edits. preview.status:complete/truncated/unavailable; unified diffs have 3 context lines. Secret redaction sets redacted:true; raw edits stay exact. preview_source(origin,sha256) identifies observed bytes, not analyzed input; analysis_freshness:unknown. supplied_version preserves integer/null only when supplied. name: get_cached_diagnostics

description: Cached diagnostics from server notifications. Faster than the pull-model diagnostics tool, no new analysis. name: get_definition
title: Go to Definition
description: Definition location of a symbol. Returns file path, line, and character where declared. Capped at a fixed maximum for a pathological case; `truncated: true` on the result means more locations exist than are returned. Aim it with `line` + `character`, or with `symbol_name` (optionally narrowed by `symbol_kind` and `container`) for a symbol defined in the file: the result then carries `resolved_symbol` with the position that was queried. A name matching several symbols, none, or an unverifiable position fails with the candidates or the reason instead of guessing. `positions_degraded` (non-UTF-16 servers only): `"request"` means the queried position was sent unconverted, so the result may describe a different symbol and should not be trusted; `"response"` means only returned `character` offsets may be inexact. Pass `context: "enclosing_symbol"` to attach `enclosing_symbol` to each item: `status` `resolved` (with `name_path`, `kind`, `range`, `fidelity`), `top_level` (no symbol contains it), `not_computed` or `unavailable` (with a `reason`; nothing is known, never read as top level). Costs one documentSymbol request per distinct file, capped per call; `enrichment` reports files enriched or skipped and `cut_short`. `out_of_workspace: true` means not provably inside a configured workspace root (lexical, advisory).

name: get_references
title: Find References
description: References in server order, including duplicates. Address with line/character or symbol_name (optional symbol_kind/container). limit: 100 by default, 1..10000. Absolute lexical path_filter selects a file or descendants before normalization. matched_count counts server-response matches; truncated means matches omitted, not complete workspace coverage. Source defaults on; include_source:false omits source work. source.status=text has text,start_line (1-based),origin (tracked/disk),shortened; unavailable has reason. Excerpts center on the starting line with up to two lines each side. Limits: 100 candidates,16 files,1 MiB/file,4 MiB read/copy,2 KiB/excerpt,64 KiB text,2 s best-effort deadline. External source is withheld. Snapshots are not atomic with LSP locations. positions_degraded=request means the queried symbol may differ; response means returned columns may be inexact. context:enclosing_symbol retains optional enclosing-symbol outcomes. out_of_workspace is lexical and advisory. Only an originally empty server response carries index_coverage.

name: rename_symbol
title: Rename Symbol
description: Propose a workspace rename by position or symbol_name. Resolve once; ambiguous names return candidates. Prepare on the rename server when supported. status:proposed has position,preparation,changes; not_renameable has no edits or preview. Preparation rejection stops rename; operational errors remain errors. Empty edits remain proposed. Nonempty dropped means incomplete: do not apply. positions_degraded:request means unreliable target; response means inexact edit columns. full defaults false; true adds exact normalized raw edits. preview.status:complete/truncated/unavailable; unified diffs have 3 context lines. Secret redaction sets redacted:true; raw edits stay exact. preview_source(origin,sha256) identifies observed bytes, not analyzed input; analysis_freshness:unknown. supplied_version preserves integer/null only when supplied. Budgets:32 files,8 MiB source+constructed text,2 s best-effort reads,100 ms off-executor diff,64 KiB display after final redaction. Limits retain edits. No writes/commands.

name: restart_server
title: Restart Server
description: Restart LSP servers: stop the old process (graceful shutdown, then a kill of its whole process group) and start a fresh one, discarding its in-memory state. Use it when a server is wedged or serves a stale index (such as after a manifest edit). Give `servers` (ids) or `all: true`. Per server, `status` is `restarted` (with `indexing_state`; `coalesced: true` if another restart of the same server just finished; `push_notifications_degraded: true` means call it again), `failed` (with a typed `reason`; the server stays registered; `refused` means nothing was stopped and the old process keeps serving, any other reason means it was stopped and the next tool call retries), `throttled` (retry after `retry_in_ms`), `initializing` or `not_running`. Requests in flight on the old process fail with a retryable error. Processes that detach into their own session may survive; shared daemons the server started (e.g. Gradle) are killed. Destructive (it kills processes the server started, which other clients may share), not read-only and not idempotent.
